newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Kia Group woes seen weighing on Seoul bourse.
newsitem.headline: Kia Group woes seen weighing on Seoul bourse.

text.p: Seoul stocks are expected to fall on Wednesday as financial troubles in the country's eighth largest business conglomerate sent interest rates higher, brokers said.
Local banks decided on Tuesday to rescue the Kia Group whose carmaking flagship has been battered by slumping sales.
"Financial institutions are scared by Kia troubles. They seem to be wondering what will happen next," said Choo Hee-yup, a broker at Dongwon Securities.
The composite index ended 9.40 points or 1.23 percent lower at 755.05 on Tuesday.
Brokers said liquidity tightened as the nation's financial community turned nervous.
Yields on three-year corporate bonds, South Korea's benchmark interest rate, rose to 11.95 percent on Tuesday from 11.87 percent on Monday.
"Institutions will tie their investment decisions to the central bank's steps to ease tightening liquidity," said Koh Kyong-bae of Hyundai Securities.
The Bank of Korea supplied one trillion won through repurchase agreements after the announcement of the Kia bail-out.
Figures from the Korea Federation of Banks showed net credit to the Kia Group by local financial institutions totalled 9.54 trillion won at the end of May.
Brokers said investors were now more concerned about possible financial troubles involving other major business groups.
The Securities Supervisory Board's probe into recent sharp rises in some smaller-capitalised shares would also dampen sentiment, they said.
